set.question: What is a 'tanya' in traditional Hungarian agricultural geography?
options: an isolated rural homestead built outside the village on farmland
a multi-storey urban apartment block built during the industrial era
a temporary military outpost established along a fortified frontier

set.question: What did the social class 'cselédség' represent in pre-1945 Hungarian rural society?
options: contract-bound farmhands living on large manorial estates with few legal rights
independent, wealthy burghers residing in prosperous chartered royal towns
university professors lecturing on modern agricultural techniques

set.question: Which pair gives each region the right ending?
Why is 'lemegy vidékre' used instead of a neutral compass direction?
options: Because Hungarian uses downward preverbs for going from the capital to the provinces.
Because all provinces in Hungary lie strictly at lower geographic elevations than Budapest.
Because it is an informal slang word banned from academic essays.
